KNOWN: Track B/II continues straight from Belorusskaya toward Krasnopresnenskaya; the turnback/depot route diverges left.
The actual Belorusskaya crossover/divergence chamber is cast-iron tubing with an RC end wall.
Moscow metro ordinary main/turnback turnout rule uses 1:9 frogs; project 2976 provides a dimensioned metro-specific R65 1:9 fallback.
Contact rail must be interrupted/sectioned as an event at the turnout rather than swept continuously.
Generic chamber 6 is a two-vault common-wall structure, not yet two independent circular running tunnels.
Current rules require event-specific evacuation passage, drainage, power boxes, emergency point lighting and clearance markers around turnouts.
CONSTRAINED: The depot/turnback area is a multi-switch system shown by published Line-5 track-development sources.
Generic stepwise chamber geometry can drive a fallback transition algorithm, but is not site-identical evidence.
Independent single-track tunnels in the generic Frolov scheme occur only after inter-track spacing exceeds 6 m; exact post-chamber-6 split chainage is not dimensioned.
Contact-rail ramp/gap/support ranges are source-backed standards, while exact local positions are unresolved.
Current drainage and evacuation geometry is normatively constrained but the historical Belorusskaya site layout is not.

A late-Soviet generic cast-iron chamber reference (S102) provides an 8.75 m / 11-tubing construction family, and a secondary Moscow reference (S103) documents cast-iron-crown + monolithic-wall/invert chambers; neither is proven as the Belorusskaya as-built geometry.
